x: Best Belgrave performances of the day were Chris Ryan's 1st in the 'C' 100yds with 10.5, Danny Wiseman's 1st in the 'B' 440yds with 51.7, Dave Cock's 2nd in the 'A' 880yds with 1:56.2 and Tony Fairclough's 2 mile win in 9:28.8.

Danny Wiseman pulled off a 440/880 double in the Junior events with Cocks - type ease, and is surely a runner of great potential. The meeting was undoubtedly a success and credit must go to Track Secretary Bob Taylor and his committee.
In the Surrey Junior Championship, Danny Wiseman succeeded Dave Cocks as holder of the 440 yards, winning the title in 51.0 . His performance entitles him to a Junior Honours Badge.
Danny Wiseman clocked 51.5 in winning the Cambridge Freshman's trials in October and in the Oxford/Cambridge Freshman's match he finished 2nd to Oxford's K.
At the Herne Hill Winter Floodlit meeting at Totting Bec on March, 25th, John Thresher won the 3,000 metres in 8.37.0 and Danny Wiseman the 660 in 82.7.
Danny Wiseman (1:53.9) and Tony Fairclough (14:25.4) again picked up valuable points but only Dabbs (30:45.0) and Black (9.37.4 s/ch) provided any noticeable support.
Danny Wiseman,who ran at the back of the field most of the way, put in a really fast finish taking him through to 6th and clocking 1:52.6 (personal best).

After qualifying fairly easily in the 'half' heats,Danny Wiseman got up to 4th in the final with 1:56.0 . He started racing rather late this season due to injuries but is now improving every time out and should be back to peak form before very long.

The half mile was terrific;Nias (HHH) just getting the verdict from Danny Wiseman,both recording 1:54.8. Danny followed this 20mins later with a win in the 440y,storming through in the straight for an easy 1st in 51.9 .
Danny Wiseman qualified for the final in the first heat of the half with no trouble in 1:56.0. In the other heat,however,Varah of Hercules took it into his head to go for a fast time.

There were high hopes that Tony Brooks might take the quarter-mile title and add his name to those past winners Dave Cocks and Danny Wiseman.

DANNY WISEMAN - the very name brings fear to the hearts of those who consider themselves 'two-lappers'. Danny got down to 1:52.2 for 880 yards some years back but then disappeared to qualify as a solicitor and then see a bit of the world.
BELGRAVE 10 MILE CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP continued. A great run as usual by Laurie but what about Danny Wiseman!

Top right: Dave Moulder the 1970 Navy Javelin champion has recently joined us and hopes to get back to his peak fitness. Bottom left: Danny Wiseman, back on the track after eight years. Bottom right: The debonair Alan Black avoids getting his feet wet again.
In the middle distances Colin Pearson improved his best 1500m time and Danny Wiseman recorded an impressive 1:54.7 in the 800m heat only to find that the 'snap' had gone when it came to the final.
It was also good to see Danny Wiseman back from wherever it is he disappears to in the winter. It's a pity we don't have his talent around more often on the country and road.
